edges.description: Altered ATPase–CW regulation and ATP-dependent dimer dynamics provide the structural model for p.Arg252Trp hyper-repression.
edges.source: Reduced ATP Hydrolysis in p.Arg252Trp MORC2

edges.description: Promoter hypermethylation is associated with reduced expression of target genes in patient-derived fibroblasts; this supports convergence with the transcriptional branch without asserting that methylation was measured in peripheral neurons.
Transcriptional alterations and axonal abnormalities coexist in variant-expressing neurons, but a causal chain through specific transcripts has not been established for CMT2Z.
Defective repair and accumulated DNA damage accompany apoptosis in the iPSC-derived motor-neuron model.
The authors link impaired DNA repair to axonal pathology; PAR restoration rescued these readouts in p.Ser87Leu neurons.
The model links excess hydroxyl radicals to increased cell death; its peripheral-neuron generalizability requires further testing.
Apoptotic loss of neurons can contribute to loss of their axons. This does not establish apoptosis as the initiating event for all axonal pathology.
intermediate_mechanisms: Loss of neuronal support and maintenance of axons

edges.description: Motor axon injury and denervation provide the clinical mechanism for spontaneous motor-unit discharges detected as fasciculations. The cited series documents their coexistence with axonal neuropathy.
Altered motor-axon excitability in the neuropathy can produce repetitive discharges detected as myokymia. This is an indirect interpretation of the electrophysiological phenotype.
intermediate_mechanisms: Altered motor-axon excitability and repetitive motor-unit discharges

edges.description: Severe motor neuropathy can compromise ventilation through respiratory-muscle weakness. This is a proposed neuromuscular explanation for the reported nocturnal hypoventilation, not a demonstrated localization of respiratory injury in that patient.
CNS involvement encompasses developmental impairment in a subset of patients; the cellular route to global delay remains unresolved.
Patient-variant human motor neurons reproduce axonal abnormalities in culture; the p.Ser87Leu line was most severely affected among the variants tested.
edges.limitations: Cultured motor neurons do not reproduce an intact motor unit, peripheral nerve environment or decades of length-dependent disease progression. The readouts measure neurite pathology in vitro.

edges.description: Inhibiting PAR degradation restored PAR levels, reduced DNA damage and improved axonal pathology in p.Ser87Leu neurons, which is a rescue rather than a description.
edges.limitations: The cited rescue was shown in p.Ser87Leu cell culture. Clinical benefit, pharmacokinetics and in vivo efficacy of this PAR-restoring intervention were not established in this report.

edges.description: Scores the cellular toxicity of a MORC2 allele as a proxy for its pathogenicity.
edges.limitations: Overexpression does not reproduce heterozygous endogenous dosage. Cortical neurons are not peripheral sensory neurons, and these toxicity assays do not measure HUSH silencing.
edges.source: MORC2 overexpression in SH-EP neuroblastoma and primary cortical neurons

edges.description: The study links protein synthesis defects to elevated hydroxyl radicals and apoptosis.
edges.limitations: The severe p.Ser87Leu allele does not represent the full CMT2Z variant spectrum. Mouse gene-transfer efficacy does not establish human benefit or delivery safety.

edges.description: AAV delivery improved the model neuropathy and muscular dysfunction.
edges.limitations: The cached abstract does not specify which individual histological endpoints were reversed; rescue of every axonal measure is not asserted.

edges.target: Reduced ATP Hydrolysis in p.Arg252Trp MORC2

evidence.reference_title: A recurrent MORC2 mutation causes Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2Z.
evidence.snippet: Pinprick was reduced to the dorsum of the foot, and joint position was normal at the toes. She was areflexic.

nodes.description: Motor and sensory axon loss underlies the peripheral neuropathy. Patient nerve biopsies show depletion of myelinated fibers and regenerative clusters. iPSC-derived motor neurons carrying disease variants develop reduced neurite length, increased breakage and axonal swellings. These culture findings complement patient pathology but do not reproduce decades of length-dependent progression.

animal_models.description: AAV delivery improved the model neuropathy and muscular dysfunction.
animal_models.name: Morc2a p.Ser87Leu heterozygous mouse

evidence.reference_title: Impaired PARP1-dependent DNA repair in MORC2 mutations drives axonal degeneration in Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease subtype 2Z and spinal muscular atrophy-like neuromotor disorders.
evidence.snippet: Our results show that MORC2 mutations induce apoptosis, DNA damage, and axonal pathology, including shortened neurites, elevated axonal breakage, and increased axonal swellings, with the most severe phenotypes observed in iPSC-MNs harboring p.S87L.

evidence.reference_title: Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease due to MORC2 mutations in Spain.
evidence.snippet: Nerve conduction studies revealed an unequivocally axonal neuropathy with frequent spontaneous activity, and serum creatine kinase levels were increased in 50% of the patients.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in the MORC2 gene cause axonal Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease.
evidence.snippet: Sural nerve biopsy revealed pronounced multifocal depletion of myelinated fibres with some regenerative clusters and occasional small onion bulbs.

evidence.reference_title: MORC2 mutations cause axonal Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease with pyramidal signs.
evidence.snippet: Nerve biopsy showed a reduction of myelinated axons of all diameters, but teased fibers showed no demyelination.

experimental_models.description: Patient-variant human motor neurons reproduce axonal abnormalities in culture; the p.Ser87Leu line was most severely affected among the variants tested.
experimental_models.name: MORC2-mutant iPSC-derived motor neurons

nodes.description: Cognitive and pyramidal features occur in some CMT2Z families. Intellectual disability was reported in 4/13 patients in the Japanese series. The responsible CNS mechanism remains uncertain; Leigh-like brain lesions and the full DIGFAN syndrome are not automatically CMT2Z manifestations.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical and mutational spectrum of Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2Z caused by MORC2 variants in Japan.
evidence.snippet: Mental retardation was identified in 4/13 patients (30.8%).

evidence.reference_title: MORC2 mutations cause axonal Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease with pyramidal signs.
evidence.snippet: The pyramidal features were usually increased muscle tone in the legs without frank spasticity, and 5 had extensor plantar reflexes.

evidence.reference_title: MORC2 mutations cause axonal Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease with pyramidal signs.
evidence.snippet: Clinically, there is pes cavus, distal muscular atrophy, and weakness of the intrinsic feet muscles, later progressing to hand muscles and finger contractures.

nodes.description: Distal weakness can progress proximally over years to decades. In the Spanish cohort, a scapuloperoneal asymmetric pattern with early proximal upper-limb involvement predominated over the classic length-dependent presentation.

evidence.reference_title: A recurrent MORC2 mutation causes Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2Z.
evidence.snippet: The neuropathy began in childhood to early adulthood, with distal weakness progressing to proximal weakness.

evidence.reference_title: Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease due to MORC2 mutations in Spain.
evidence.snippet: Eleven patients were categorized as having a scapuloperoneal phenotype, with asymmetric muscle weakness, early proximal upper limb involvement and frequent spontaneous muscular activity with distal sensory impairment and pes cavus, whilst two presented with a more classic length dependent sensory motor phenotype.

nodes.description: Distal sensory loss accompanies the motor neuropathy, although clinical sensory impairment varies and may be mild or absent despite sensory nerve conduction abnormalities.

evidence.reference_title: Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease due to MORC2 mutations in Spain.
evidence.snippet: frequent spontaneous muscular activity with distal sensory impairment and pes cavus

nodes.description: The recurrent p.Arg252Trp variant accelerates and increases HUSH-dependent repression in HeLa reporter assays and over-represses endogenous target genes in SK-N-SH neuroblastoma cells. MORC2 is recruited by HUSH to support chromatin compaction; SETDB1 deposits H3K9me3. This measured gain in cellular silencing does not mean that MORC2 ATP hydrolysis is increased, and it is not established for every MORC2 variant.

evidence.reference_title: Hyperactivation of HUSH complex function by Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease mutation in MORC2.
evidence.snippet: The ATPase activity of MORC2 is critical for HUSH-mediated silencing, and the most common alteration affecting the ATPase domain in CMT patients (p.Arg252Trp) hyperactivates HUSH-mediated repression in neuronal cells.

nodes.description: Fasciculations were recorded on needle electromyography in the founding MORC2 neuropathy series.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in the MORC2 gene cause axonal Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease.
evidence.snippet: Electrophysiological studies were consistent with an asymmetric axonal motor and sensory neuropathy, while fasciculations and myokymia were recorded rather frequently by needle electromyography.

nodes.description: The Spanish collection included two patients with a neurodevelopmental presentation and delayed motor milestones; global developmental delay was reported in one of them.

evidence.reference_title: Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease due to MORC2 mutations in Spain.
evidence.snippet: Two other patients were classified as having a neurodevelopmental phenotype consisting in congenital or early onset, delay in motor milestones, and global developmental delay in one of them.

nodes.description: The Morc2a p.Ser87Leu mouse study linked reduced protein synthesis and loss of function to elevated hydroxyl radicals and apoptosis. It also examined mouse embryonic fibroblasts and human p.Arg252Trp fibroblasts. This model supports an oxidative-damage route, whose relationship to HUSH-mediated silencing and PARP1 repair remains unresolved.

animal_models.description: The study links protein synthesis defects to elevated hydroxyl radicals and apoptosis.
animal_models.name: Morc2a p.Ser87Leu heterozygous mouse

evidence.reference_title: Morc2a variants cause hydroxyl radical-mediated neuropathy and are rescued by restoring GHKL ATPase.
evidence.snippet: This study revealed that Morc2a p.S87L causes a protein synthesis defect, resulting in the loss of function of Morc2a and high cellular apoptosis induced by high hydroxyl radical levels.

nodes.description: In human iPSC-derived motor neurons carrying p.Ser87Leu, p.Gln400Arg or p.Asp466Asn, mutant MORC2 impairs its interaction with PARP1, reduces PARP1 activity and expression, and diminishes DNA-repair protein expression and recruitment. This cellular mechanism has not been established as a downstream consequence of HUSH hyper-repression.

evidence.reference_title: Impaired PARP1-dependent DNA repair in MORC2 mutations drives axonal degeneration in Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease subtype 2Z and spinal muscular atrophy-like neuromotor disorders.
evidence.snippet: Mechanistically, these mutations impair DNA repair by disrupting the interaction between MORC2 and PARP1, leading to reduced PARP1 activity and expression, as well as diminished DNA repair protein expression and recruitment.

experimental_models.description: Inhibiting PAR degradation restored PAR levels, reduced DNA damage and improved axonal pathology in p.Ser87Leu neurons, which is a rescue rather than a description.
experimental_models.name: MORC2-mutant iPSC-derived motor neurons

nodes.description: Cognitive impairment was present in about a third of the Japanese CMT2Z cohort. The authors single it out as under-recognised and mechanistically unexplained. At the ATPase-module end of the MORC2 spectrum it is part of a fuller neurodevelopmental syndrome.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical and mutational spectrum of Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2Z caused by MORC2 variants in Japan.
evidence.snippet: Mental retardation was identified in 4/13 patients (30.8%).

evidence.reference_title: Clinical and mutational spectrum of Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2Z caused by MORC2 variants in Japan.
evidence.snippet: p.Arg190Trp, as a mutational hotspot, was observed in eight unrelated families.

evidence.reference_title: Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease due to MORC2 mutations in Spain.
evidence.snippet: The most common mutation was p.R252W, and four new mutations were identified.

evidence.reference_title: Hyperactivation of HUSH complex function by Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease mutation in MORC2.
evidence.snippet: an arginine to tryptophan substitution at residue 252 (R252W or p.Arg252Trp in Uniprot: Q9Y6X9-1) ... This is the identical mutation to the reported R190W variant ... which refers to a putative alternative isoform of the protein (Uniprot: Q9Y6X9-2) that lacks 62 amino acids at the N-terminus.

evidence.reference_title: A recurrent MORC2 mutation causes Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2Z.
evidence.snippet: More than 20 different mutations in MORC2 cause Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2Z (CMT2Z), a dominantly inherited axonal neuropathy

evidence.reference_title: Novel MORC2 variants in Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2Z: genetic and functional insights.
evidence.snippet: In each family, we identified a different heterozygous variant in the MORC2 gene, namely c.34G > C;p.A12P in family 1 and c.848G > A;p.R283H in family 2. ... Both variants were therefore classified as likely pathogenic.

evidence.reference_title: Novel MORC2 variants in Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2Z: genetic and functional insights.
evidence.snippet: In their study, this variant did not co-segregate with the disease and was therefore not included in the HGMD database.

nodes.description: MORC2 variants were expressed in SH-EP neuroblastoma cells and primary embryonic mouse cortical neurons. Survival, cleaved caspase-3 and neurite length supplied functional evidence alongside family and clinical findings.
nodes.id: MORC2 overexpression in SH-EP neuroblastoma and primary cortical neurons

evidence.reference_title: Expanding the phenotypic variability of MORC2 gene mutations: From Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease to late-onset pure motor neuropathy.
evidence.snippet: Likewise, we show that MORC2 mutants affect survival and trigger apoptosis over time in SH-EP cell line. Furthermore, overexpression in primary cortical neurons increases apoptotic cell death and decreases neurite outgrowth.

nodes.description: Human iPSC-derived motor neurons carrying p.Ser87Leu, associated with an SMA-like phenotype, and p.Gln400Arg or p.Asp466Asn, associated with CMT2Z, permit comparison of cellular effects across the MORC2 spectrum.

evidence.reference_title: Impaired PARP1-dependent DNA repair in MORC2 mutations drives axonal degeneration in Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease subtype 2Z and spinal muscular atrophy-like neuromotor disorders.
evidence.snippet: we used iPSC-derived motor neurons (iPSC-MNs) carrying three distinct MORC2 mutations, p.S87L (SMA-like), p.Q400R, and p.D466N (CMT2Z), to examine their effects on cellular processes

nodes.description: The p.Ser87Leu mouse models neuropathy and muscular dysfunction associated with DNA damage and hydroxyl radical accumulation. AAV-PHP.eB delivery of Morc2a or its GHKL ATPase domain improved neuropathy and muscular dysfunction after one treatment.

evidence.reference_title: Morc2a variants cause hydroxyl radical-mediated neuropathy and are rescued by restoring GHKL ATPase.
evidence.snippet: We used the adeno-associated virus (AAV)-PHP.eB serotype, which has a high CNS transduction efficiency, to express Morc2a or Morc2a GHKL ATPase domain protein in vivo. Notably, AAV gene therapy ameliorated neuropathy and muscular dysfunction with a single treatment.

evidence.snippet: Electrophysiological studies were consistent with an asymmetric axonal motor and sensory neuropathy, while fasciculations and myokymia were recorded rather frequently by needle electromyography.

nodes.description: MORC2-variant overexpression increases apoptotic cell death in primary mouse cortical neurons, and patient-variant iPSC motor-neuron models also show apoptosis. These are cellular findings across CMT and related MORC2 phenotypes.

evidence.snippet: He began using a wheelchair at age 18 years, became wheelchair dependent at 25 years, and began using BiPAP at age 28 years for nocturnal hypoventilation.

nodes.description: Blood and fibroblast profiling across MORC2-related phenotypes identified an episignature dominated by promoter hypermethylation. CMT patients had elevated ERCC8–NDUFAF2 promoter methylation relative to controls, with a larger effect in mitochondrial disease. Binding-site overlap suggests that much of this signature is HUSH-independent; no direct HUSH-to-promoter-methylation edge is asserted.

biological_processes: negative regulation of gene expression via chromosomal CpG island methylation

evidence.reference_title: Pleiotropic effects of MORC2 derive from its epigenetic signature.
evidence.snippet: Mitochondrial disease patients exhibited significantly higher methylation levels than those with CMT, while CMT patients still demonstrated significantly elevated methylation levels relative to controls

evidence.reference_title: Pleiotropic effects of MORC2 derive from its epigenetic signature.
evidence.snippet: Overall, this suggests that although some of the effects of mutant MORC2 on DNA methylation are mediated through interactions with the HUSH complex, the majority are driven by the HUSH-independent function of MORC2.

nodes.description: Pyramidal signs vary between and within MORC2 genotypes. The original p.Arg252Trp CMT105 family included increased leg tone without frank spasticity and extensor plantar responses. These signs were absent in the three p.Ala406Val patients reported by Vujovic and colleagues.

evidence.reference_title: MORC2 mutations cause axonal Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease with pyramidal signs.
evidence.snippet: The pyramidal features were usually increased muscle tone in the legs without frank spasticity, and 5 had extensor plantar reflexes.

nodes.description: Purified MORC2(1–603) carrying the CMT2Z p.Arg252Trp variant has modestly reduced ATP hydrolysis. Structural analysis proposes disruption of the regulatory ATPase–CW interface, with altered dimer dynamics explaining increased cellular silencing despite reduced hydrolysis. The molecular-function decrease is specific to this tested allele and construct.
nodes.id: Reduced ATP Hydrolysis in p.Arg252Trp MORC2

evidence.reference_title: Neuropathic MORC2 mutations perturb GHKL ATPase dimerization dynamics and epigenetic silencing by multiple structural mechanisms
evidence.snippet: The R252W MORC2 variant hyperactivates HUSH-mediated transgene silencing4, but has reduced ATPase activity in vitro.

evidence.reference_title: Neuropathic MORC2 mutations perturb GHKL ATPase dimerization dynamics and epigenetic silencing by multiple structural mechanisms
evidence.snippet: T424R, which hydrolyzes ATP more rapidly than wild- type, leads to less ef ﬁcient HUSH silencing, whereas S87L and R252W, which hydrolyze ATP more slowly than wild-type, match or hyperactivate wild-type HUSH silencing

nodes.description: MORC2 variants alter gene expression through HUSH-dependent repression and promoter DNA hypermethylation. p.Arg252Trp and p.Ser87Leu alter transcription in patient fibroblasts and rodent sensory-neuron expression models. Separately, fibroblast profiling across the MORC2 spectrum identified reduced ERCC8, NDUFAF2 and FKTN transcripts. These named target changes were measured in fibroblasts; their contribution to peripheral-neuron pathology is not established.

evidence.reference_title: Characterization of molecular mechanisms underlying the axonal Charcot-Marie-Tooth neuropathy caused by MORC2 mutations.
evidence.snippet: These changes were more pronounced and accompanied by abnormal axonal morphology, in neurons expressing the MORC2 p.S87L mutation, which is associated with a more severe clinical phenotype.

evidence.reference_title: Characterization of molecular mechanisms underlying the axonal Charcot-Marie-Tooth neuropathy caused by MORC2 mutations.
evidence.snippet: Both mutations induced transcriptional changes in patient-derived fibroblasts and when expressed in rodent sensory neurons.

evidence.reference_title: Pleiotropic effects of MORC2 derive from its epigenetic signature.
evidence.snippet: Three of the four genes—ERCC8, NDUFAF2 and FKTN—were also identified as recurrent expression outliers in MORC2 patients, with reduced expression levels typical of monogenic disorders caused by primary mutations in these genes

evidence.reference_title: Pleiotropic effects of MORC2 derive from its epigenetic signature.
evidence.snippet: When comparing mitochondrial respiration, the fibroblast cell line from a CMT patient exhibited an intermediate phenotype, falling between that of a Leigh syndrome patient with CI deficiency and a healthy control

nodes.description: A 2026 Chinese family study classified both variants as likely pathogenic, reporting p.Ala12Pro protein instability and reduced p.Arg283His transcript abundance in transfected HEK293T cells. p.Arg283His failed segregation in an earlier family, so the newer segregating family and functional results should be considered alongside that conflicting evidence.
Reported in three individuals from two families with severe neuropathy progressing from distal to proximal weakness.

Recurrent CMT2Z variant that hyperactivates HUSH-mediated repression in neuronal cell models. Early distal weakness and sensory loss can progress proximally. The same variant was reported as p.Arg190Trp in eight unrelated Japanese families using the shorter protein isoform.

p.Gly444Arg segregated in a family with adult-onset sensorimotor CMT, while p.His446Gln was found in a separate patient with adult pure motor neuropathy. Overexpression assays supported deleterious effects of both variants, alongside the clinical evidence; the pure motor presentation is an allelic comparison rather than a CMT2Z subtype.

Associated with severe early-onset neuropathy with SMA-like features. It produced greater transcriptional changes and axonal abnormalities than p.Arg252Trp in the compared neuronal-expression system, and the most severe pathology among the variants tested in the cited iPSC motor-neuron study.
